notes: Every tool must be free ($0). Verify: Sha256 where the vendor publishes a hash; Authenticode where it does not; TransportOnly (HTTPS) only as a last resort with an explicit warning. Manual items are dropped into <StageRoot>/inbox/ by the operator.

tools.Name: Kaspersky Rescue Disk
tools.Notes: Reference SHA-256 for 18.0.11.3d (mirror copy, Jan 2025). Refresh against the official support page at staging time; a mismatch is a hard abort. US customers: official US downloads are blocked — use the non-US support page or a reputable mirror, the checksum is what vouches for the file.
tools.RunsFrom: Bootable ISO entry on Phoenix USB

tools.Name: Sysinternals Suite
tools.Notes: Microsoft publishes no hash for the suite ZIP; verify the Authenticode signature of the extracted binaries instead. Key tools for this kit: Autoruns (offline-system mode), Sigcheck, Process Explorer, Process Monitor, TCPView.

tools.License: Free for PRIVATE USE ONLY (commercial use requires EEK Pro)
tools.Name: Emsisoft Emergency Kit
tools.Notes: Self-extracting portable scanner (GUI + command line). License covers Brandon's personal laptop triage; any DOGS-company client work needs the Pro license.

tools.License: Proprietary freeware (free registration required to download)
tools.Name: FTK Imager (free edition)
tools.Notes: No stable direct download URL (registration gate), so the operator drops the installer into inbox/ and the stager verifies its signature. Do NOT substitute the paid FTK Imager Pro ($499) — the free edition covers imaging, mounting, extraction, and hashing.

tools.Name: Autopsy
tools.Notes: Heavy forensics platform — never goes on the boot USB. GitHub releases publish no checksum for the MSI, so integrity rests on HTTPS transport from the official repo; if the filename 404s, check https://www.autopsy.com/download/ for the current release and update this entry.
tools.RunsFrom: Staging machine ONLY (8GB RAM min, 16GB recommended, Java 11+)
